data.narrative:
Lila Sciences is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Geoffrey von Maltzahn and Molly Gibson that has raised $200M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in the sector, though narrow peer matching proved limited for direct comparison.

Only the stage-progression method yielded a reliable result given available data constraints. Applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $200M total raised proxy generates an implied valuation of $400M. The peer-median method was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum sample thresholds (fewer than 3 datapoints met filtering criteria). Public comp anchoring could not be applied because target revenue is not disclosed; while the Biotech & Health median P/S stands at 8.1x across the 3 public tickers, private companies rarely report revenue, preventing multiple application.

The triangulated range supported by available evidence is $340M to $460M, with a median of $400M. This range rests on a single methodology, however, creating material uncertainty. Key risks to valuation include: unknown revenue or cash-burn profile; lack of granular stage-specific peer data; and absence of disclosed milestones or clinical progress. Further diligence on pipeline maturity, cash runway, and competitive positioning would be necessary to narrow the range.
